jobDescription: A payments company screens card-not-present transactions for its e-commerce merchants with an in-house fraud model. The fraud analytics lead is the accountable owner of that model, approves threshold changes, builds features from authorisation data, works with fraud operations on alert tuning and presents performance to the model risk committee. The model moves to a new real-time scoring service next year, and experience building or running such a service would help. The fraud analytics team has five data scientists and reports to the chief risk officer.
requirements: Is the accountable owner of a fraud-detection model, approving threshold changes.
Builds fraud features from transaction and authorisation data.
Works with fraud operations on rule and alert tuning.
Presents model performance to the model risk committee.
Has built or operated a real-time model-scoring service.

evidence.text: Fraud data scientist, then fraud analytics lead, at Corvane Payments from 2018 to 2024, working on card-not-present fraud detection for e-commerce merchants in the UK and Ireland.
Built velocity and device-consistency features from authorisation data, tested each on a holdout month and documented each one in the feature catalogue.
Approved two changes to the decline threshold in 2023 after weekly reviews with the fraud operations manager; both are recorded in the model change log.

Presented the half-yearly performance review of the card-not-present model (detection rate, false-positive rate and alert volumes) to the model risk committee, with the threshold history and the changes planned for the next half-year.
Reviewed the scoring service's latency reports with the platform team, which built and ran the real-time scoring service, and raised two tickets when response times drifted above the agreed limit.
Work sample: the model change log entry for the October 2023 decline-threshold change, with the supporting analysis, the fraud operations manager's comments and the candidate's approval.

Recruiter verification: the former employer's model risk team confirmed in writing that the model inventory lists the candidate as accountable model owner for the card-not-present fraud model from 2022 to 2024.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate has a one-month notice period, is available for interviews on Wednesdays and would like to meet the fraud operations manager.
